notes.meaning: A guilty conscience fills wrongdoers with dread, making them run even when nobody is chasing them. In contrast, those who walk rightly with God have a clear conscience and quiet trust in Him, which gives them the courage of a lion. God gives His people boldness because they know He is their protector.

When a nation turns to sin and rebellion, its government often breaks down into chaos, with rival leaders fighting for control. But God preserves a society when wise and understanding leaders govern with justice. Good leadership brings lasting peace and stability to a country.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars note that the phrase for maintaining order is difficult to translate, and the many rulers may refer to rapid successions of kings, similar to the period of the judges.

notes.meaning: A needy person who gains authority and abuses other poor people does great damage. Instead of showing pity based on his own past hardships, his greed washes away everything like a destructive storm that ruins crops. Power given to the selfish leaves the vulnerable with nothing.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars suggest the original text meant a wicked ruler rather than a destitute leader, because the poor rarely held the power to oppress others.

notes.meaning: People who abandon God's law start calling evil good and cheer on other wrongdoers. But those who love and obey God's commands cannot remain silent; they speak out against sin and oppose wickedness. Keeping God's word gives us the moral clarity to stand up for what is right.

People blinded by selfish desires lose the ability to tell right from wrong. In contrast, those who seek the Lord through prayer and His word receive spiritual wisdom to understand what is truly fair. Drawing near to God opens our minds to His truth.

Living an honest life pleasing to God is far better than having great wealth gained through deceit. A person with integrity may lack money, but he has peace with God, whereas a crooked rich man lives a double life. True worth comes from godly character, not from earthly possessions.

A son who listens to God's law and his parents' instructions shows true wisdom. But a child who runs with reckless, wasteful companions brings shame and grief to his whole family. Choosing good company protects both our character and our family's honor.

People who grow rich by taking unfair advantage of the poor and charging harsh interest will not keep their gains. In God's providence, that ill-gotten wealth will eventually pass into the hands of generous people who care for those in need. God ensures that greed does not have the final say.

When someone refuses to listen to God's word and obey His commands, God rejects that person's prayers. Prayer cannot be used as a mask for willful disobedience. God desires our sincere obedience before He welcomes our petitions.

Anyone who plots to drag godly people into sin will end up trapped in the ruin he prepared for them. Meanwhile, God protects the blameless and rewards them with lasting blessings. Evil schemes ultimately destroy the schemer.

Wealth often tricks people into thinking they are smarter and better than everyone else. Yet a poor person with godly insight can look right through the rich man's pride and see his true lack of wisdom. True insight is a gift from God, not something money can buy.

When godly leaders prosper and rule, the whole community celebrates and flourishes in freedom. But when corrupt leaders take control, good people retreat into hiding to escape harm and injustice. Righteous government brings honor and safety to everyone.

Trying to hide or make excuses for our sins only leads to spiritual ruin and a burdened heart. True relief comes when we openly admit our wrongs to God and turn away from them in genuine repentance. God readily offers His free mercy and forgiveness to all who come clean before Him.

The person who lives with a healthy, watchful fear of God and an aversion to sin finds true peace and safety. But someone who stubbornly shuts his heart to God's warnings will stumble straight into ruin. Keeping a tender conscience protects us from spiritual disaster.

A cruel, corrupt ruler behaves like a hungry, predatory beast let loose on defenseless prey. Instead of shielding his subjects like a caring shepherd, he uses his strength to exploit and harm them. Leaders are called to protect the weak, not prey upon them.

A ruler without understanding thinks he can enrich himself by crushing his subjects under heavy burdens, but this foolishness ruins his reign. On the other hand, a ruler who despises dishonest gain and bribery earns the loyalty of his people and enjoys a long, secure rule. Wise leaders value justice far above wealth.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars read this verse not merely as a general observation, but as a direct warning addressed to a foolish ruler.

notes.meaning: A murderer is pursued by the torment of his own guilty conscience and divine justice until death overtakes him. God's law forbade sheltering or excusing someone guilty of intentional bloodshed, because life is sacred. No one should interfere with the proper demands of justice against murder.

A person who lives honestly and sincerely before God walks under divine protection. But a hypocrite who tries to balance two crooked ways will collapse without warning. Sincerity of heart brings real security in times of trouble.

Faithful, steady labor produces enough food to support a home and share with others. In contrast, someone who wastes time chasing get-rich-quick schemes will end up stuffed with nothing but poverty. Diligence leads to plenty, while foolish dreams lead to want.

A trustworthy person who deals honestly and honors his commitments receives rich blessings from both God and people. But someone consumed by the rush to get rich quickly easily falls into dishonest schemes and brings judgment on himself. True lasting prosperity comes through patience and integrity.

Showing favoritism in judgment undermines justice and violates God's law. Once a judge or leader begins taking bribes, he becomes so corrupt that even the smallest reward can tempt him to do wrong. Justice must always treat everyone fairly without regard to status or personal gain.

A greedy and envious person is obsessed with gathering riches for himself and refuses to help others. Because he ignores God's laws of generosity and honesty, he fails to realize that sudden ruin and poverty are heading his way. Selfish hoarding ultimately empties the hands of the hoarder.

Giving a loving, honest correction may sting at first, but the person corrected will later appreciate the true friend who helped him change. A flatterer only uses smooth words to win favor, which helps no one in the end. Faithful honesty builds deeper trust than empty compliments.

Taking property from aging parents under the excuse that it will someday be inherited is still theft. Anyone who treats their parents this way adds cold ingratitude and disrespect to the crime of stealing. God views such callous behavior as no better than violent robbery.

A proud and greedy person constantly causes arguments because he always wants more for himself and cannot stand competition. But the person who relies quietly on the Lord experiences true contentment and flourishing under God's care. Trusting God frees us from the endless rat race of selfish ambition.

Relying entirely on our own feelings, understanding, and self-righteousness is foolish, because the human heart is easily deceived. Safety is found instead by walking in godly wisdom, listening to wise counsel, and fearing the Lord. Leaning on God's truth keeps us from dangerous missteps.

God promises that generous people who share with the poor will never suffer lack because of their kindness. But those who deliberately ignore suffering and look away from people in need will face harsh curses and God's displeasure. Compassion opens the door to God's blessing.

When corrupt leaders take control, honest and godly citizens retreat from public life to avoid harm. But when evil rulers are removed, righteous people step forward again, and godliness and freedom spread through the land. Good leadership allows the entire community to thrive.
